brief: September nonfarm payrolls rose 29k, far below the 90k consensus, with prior months revised down a cumulative 60k. That pulls the three-month moving average to 51k, which PNC says is roughly the pace needed to hold the unemployment rate stable, since slower labor force growth and weaker immigration have lowered the breakeven level. Private payrolls added 46k, as weakness in local government hiring dragged the headline total down. The unemployment rate rose to 4.18% (rounds to 4.2%) from 4.14% in August, driven by higher labor force participation rather than weaker hiring, and PNC calls this consistent with the Fed's view of full employment. Underemployment fell to 7.6% from 7.7%. Average hourly earnings rose at a 1.6% annualized pace, pulling six-month annualized wage growth to 2.5%, below pre-pandemic levels, so PNC says labor is not yet an inflation source, even as rising hours keep aggregate payroll income growing near 5%. PNC calls this a dovish report that keeps the Fed on hold in October, but still expects the underlying trend to be stable-to-reaccelerating, and expects two more hikes, in December and March, driven by coming inflation prints.
